Nine warm-toned rings arranged around a vertical axis, opening and closing like a flower around a glowing core. Each ring reads the same opening cosine with its own phase offset, so the opening travels around the whorl. Drag to turn it.

Four concentric rings of text turning at rational multiples of one rate, against a fixed tick ring. Because the ratios are fixed, the rings keep arriving at the same relative positions and words line up on the vertical before drifting apart again.

A banknote rosette: six nested hypotrochoid curves in blue and brown hairlines, framed by plain rules. Each curve is one equation of two rolling circles, run for enough turns to fill its band with lacework.

A harmonograph figure drawing itself: two decaying sine pairs per axis, with a bright pen at the growing end of the trace and the completed figure showing faintly behind it. The curve grows because the drawn interval grows, not because anything is remembered between frames.

A torus drawn as a wireframe grid, tumbling slowly. Every edge of the mesh is submitted on every frame and the back half is hidden by the surface's own front faces, so edges wink out as they cross the silhouette. Drag to turn it.

Two identical sets of concentric circles with their centres slightly apart. The broad dark bands sweeping across the square are moire fringes — interference between the two sets, not drawn by anything in the document. Drag to pull the centres further apart and crowd the fringes together.

An armillary sphere: four slender rings at different inclinations, each precessing about its own axis, with small bodies running round three of them and a warm lamp at the centre lighting their inner faces. Drag to turn it.

A sunflower seed head of nine hundred florets, dark olive at the centre and gold at the rim. Each floret sits at the golden angle from the one before it, at a radius proportional to the square root of its index; the interlocking spirals are not drawn but fall out of that placement. The divergence angle drifts a fraction of a degree either side of golden, and the spiral families unwind and re-form as it passes through.

A pipe of shaded metallic balls running in straight stretches and square corners, coiling toward the viewer and growing longer as time passes, in the manner of the old Pipes screensaver. The pipe is drawn in two dimensions; the depth is a hand-written perspective divide, and the pipe grows because the drawing loop's bound is an expression in the clock.

Six rose curves of three to nine petals, drawn over one another in a cool-to-warm ramp. Each turns at its own rate and breathes in radius, so the figure continuously re-composes. Every curve is a single formula sampled by the renderer.

A corridor of twenty square frames rushing toward the viewer and twisting as it recedes, lit from a point source down its axis. The frames never spawn or retire: each one's depth wraps on a modulo, so the corridor has no end and no state. Drag to roll it.

Five ceramic vessels in a dark vitrine, each one a surface of revolution defined entirely by a short list of radius and height points: a flared hourglass, a stack of lobes, an unsettling set of shelves, a wide saucer on a thin neck, and a pear with a floating bulb. Drag to turn the row.
